_meta.what_this_is: A/B results for two agent harnesses on a 15-instance SWE-bench slice: 'vanilla' (a plain coding agent) vs 'omc' (the same agent under an orchestration layer). Each instance was attempted K=3 times per system; each attempt either resolved the issue (its hidden test suite passes) or did not. The question of this capstone: does omc help, and can you defend the answer with an interval?
_meta.THESE_OUTCOMES_ARE_A_FIXTURE: CRITICAL: the resolved/not-resolved values here are ILLUSTRATIVE, hand-authored to stand in for one real run, exactly as the earlier modules used stored model outputs. They are NOT a real SWE-bench evaluation of these instances, and must never be cited as one. The instance ids use the real SWE-bench Lite format only so the slice reads concretely; the numbers are synthetic. Running the real harness to produce your own results.json is the hand-off (see the module's Build section).
_meta.why_the_test_suite_is_the_oracle: SWE-bench needs no LLM judge: an attempt 'resolved' the instance iff the repository's own hidden test suite passes after the patch. That deterministic oracle is why this capstone does not calibrate a judge (evals-inter-02) -- the gold label is the tests.
_meta.resolved_true_means: the hidden test suite passed after this attempt's patch
